text: APIs, or Application Programming Interfaces, allow different software systems to communicate with each other. When you work with an API, your program typically sends an HTTP request—such as GET to retrieve data or POST to send new information. Most modern APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy for computers to read and convert into usable objects. However, secure APIs often require authentication, usually through an API key or a token, so the server knows who is making the request. You must also respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a given time period. Finally, always implement proper error handling, as servers may return errors like "404 Not Found" or "429 Too Many Requests," and your code should respond gracefully without crashing.
